findings.summary: This was raised in the last review and is still not fixed. At phone width, every table keeps its desktop columns and scrolls sideways inside its box, with nothing to show that more columns exist. The last visible column ends exactly at the border, so each table looks complete. On the security screen, the sessions table shows only Device and Location: Last active and every Revoke row action are off-screen, so the screen's main task can't be seen. The overview and project tables stop at Status, which hides Budget and Due date. The team table stops at Role, which hides Location and Active projects. On both the team and security tables, cell text runs into the right border. This happens in light and dark.
findings.promptFix: Under breakpoint.md, a table never silently hides columns at phone width, and this rule is part of building the table component, not an afterthought. If any row has an action, or the table has more than three columns, reflow each row at the phone breakpoint into a stacked block inside the same bordered box. The primary cell is the block's title, every other cell becomes a label/value line, and the row action sits visible at the end of the block. Sideways scroll inside the box is allowed only for a read-only table of three or four short columns. In that case, size the columns so the last visible one is cut part-way at the edge, and keep space.12 of padding between cell text and the border. Add a required Verification step: at 390px, in each theme, check that every row action is on screen without scrolling the table, that every column's data is either visible or clearly cut off at the edge, and that no cell text touches the border. If any check fails, the build is not done.

findings.summary: This was raised in the last review and is still not fixed. In the desktop empty-filter state, the band's always-visible pink 'Refresh' and the empty state's pink 'Clear filters' are on screen together, in light and dark. That makes two pink actions in one viewport, which breaks the one-pink-action rule the reference is built around.
findings.promptFix: Choose pink per state, not per component. An action that stays on screen in a page header, band or toolbar (refresh, export, share, settings) is always lift--ink or lift--ghost, never pink, whatever state the page is in. Pink goes only to the one action the current state is about: the form submit, an empty-state or error recovery, a dialog confirm, or the page's main CTA. A component that brings its own button (empty state, error panel, toast) may make it pink only when no other pink button can be in the same viewport. Add a required Verification step: render every captured state at the desktop viewport in each theme and count the pink-filled buttons. There must be at most one, not counting small price or status tags. If any state shows two, the build is not done.

findings.summary: The save confirmation on the settings form shows as an inline chip after the form buttons, with a button's border and hard offset shadow, instead of the fixed toast the spec describes. Next to a lifted save button it reads as a third button, not as a status message.

The dashboard's empty-filter state uses a small, icon-sized magnifier instead of the one size.stickerLg sticker that the spec's empty-state row asks for. It reads as a plain icon message, while the blog's and the cart's empty states show the full sticker.

notes: Review: 131/131 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.4/review-2).
Review: 131/131 checklist items by 8 reviewers and the lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.4/review-2). I opened the card-hover and tote product-page screenshots myself.
No blockers. The hidden table columns and Revoke actions can still be reached by swiping inside the table, so the task is hidden, not broken. Nothing overlaps, and the reference's identity holds.

Merged: the dashboard reviewer's major (overview, project and team tables hide columns at phone width) and the settings reviewer's major (the sessions table hides Revoke) are the same broken rule, so they are one major caused by the spec. The fix makes table reflow part of building the table, with a required check at 390px.

Resolved since review 1: linked product cards now lift on hover. I opened the capture: the first card moves up-left and has a hard ink offset shadow. This run is the same build as review 1, re-shot after the change to the capture tool (shoot.ts), so the earlier 'no lift' was at least partly a capture problem, not a build problem.

Not re-raised (earlier minors): product detail pages don't mark the 'Shop' pill as current. I confirmed in the tote capture that 'Shop' is plain text. rc.3 raised this as a minor, and review 1 of rc.4 wrongly listed it as fixed. The spec's contradiction on pink versus ink for switches that are on (rc.3 minor) is still in the spec. The coin sticker's outline turning white in dark mode, the dark row-hover fill and the clipped focus ring in the pill strip were all raised in review 1.
Regressions: none. The dashboard's two pink actions are carried over from review 1, not new.

The four apps look like one family. They share paper and ink, regular-weight display type, one full-width color band per section with an ink rule under it, ink current-page pills (paper-filled in dark), outlined cards, pink price tags, the same dark mapping and the same focus treatment (ink ring in light, pink ring in dark).

Someone who knows the reference would recognize it. The yellow hero has tilted, edge-cropped coin stickers. The shop is a flooded yellow band over a dense wall of different sticker products on band-color squares. Linked cards now get the hard lift.
Signature elements: bands, outline pills, sticker art and the hard lift (now on buttons and cards) hold across all apps. The one remaining signature break is the always-on pink Refresh.
Not passing: two majors. Phone-width tables hide columns and row actions (caused by the spec), and the dashboard shows two pink actions in one viewport (carried over).
